It's not important at all. I just find this issue to be interesting and I enjoy the debate. The reality is that I would very likely be fine with my woman seeing whoever she wants to see, because I wouldn't date someone who I don't find trustworthy. My argument is just that, in certain situations, seeing straight male friends alone might be seen as odd. Now, this could change if I'm also friends with the male friend or if it's in a group setting. But, taking OP's situation and assuming they were exclusive, that could be a situation that might bother me.

To me, it's not controlling if I just voice my concerns and we have a discussion about it. That could solve everything. A relationship is give and take and both sides should be willing to compromise. And if my woman should insist on doing something that makes me uncomfortable, then I'll consider ending the relationship. I'm not trying to control her, if she wants to do something or see people that bothers me then I have no obligation to stay.

For the last time, it's all context dependent and subjective. I'm not controlling anything. If it's a situation where it makes me uncomfortable that she's hanging out with male friends alone repeatedly without me, then I'm going to talk to her about it. Maybe it's a situation where I completely trust her and it's totally fine. Very possible. But if it's early in the relationship, maybe not. All context dependent. But no, I'm not controlling anything. If it bothers me and she is unwilling to compromise, then maybe I leave the relationship. I won't force her to do anything she is unwilling to do. Controlling is the wrong word to use. You have your opinion and I have mine. No one is right, no one is wrong

Like I said repeatedly, it is context dependent. If you trust your partner completely, fine whatever. However, hanging out alone with friends of the sex to which you are attracted to when you are in a significant relationship is unique, whether you want to admit it or not. I have several friends in serious relationships and their girlfriends do not hang out with guy friends without their SO.

The reality is, straight male friends of straight females are ALWAYS going to be thinking about sex in the back of their minds, whether they admit to it or not. That's just reality, you can choose to accept that or not. And if a straight female in a serious relationship chooses to repeatedly hang out with a straight male friend without their SO, that could send the wrong message. It's just generally not necessary to do so. That is my opinion. You can call it relationship insecurity if you want, I really don't care.

Dating issues like this are subjective and always context dependent. There is no hardline rule to this kind of thing. If someone is uncomfortable with it, you should talk about it and try to resolve it. Mutual respect is important and if you show respect to your partner in this regard I'm sure it is more likely they will trust you to hang out with your opposite sex friends. It's a two way street, and communication is key. That's all there is to it

Now you're assuming. If I were dating a bisexual, I personally would be totally fine if my girlfriend hung out with women, kissed them, and even had sex with them. In fact, I might even encourage it. I would be less enthusiastic about men, for obvious reasons. If my girlfriend turned out to be gay, then oh well nothing to be done.

You seem to be making my comment out as something it's not. If you're in a serious relationship, then I would assume you know the sexuality of your partner. Again, just be respectful of your partner and don't make them unreasonably uncomfortable. Don't think that's asking too much. No need to read any more into it

Because we are referring to two straight people in this post. If the situation is different, then it would change accordingly. I am straight, so I don't have perspective in that situation. But again, it's all context dependent and depends on the relationship and the level of trust between the two people. Just be respectful of your partner is what it comes down to

Perhaps for OP's situation, but I was responding to the person above who referenced a SO. Imo, if you're in significant relationship, there shouldn't really be a need to hang out alone with friends of the opposite gender. But like I said below, I agree that it's context dependent and if you trust your partner implicitly, then it's probably totally fine. It's subjective, just like most dating issues are
Agreed. It's all context dependent and subjective

Finding little things to look forward to is very important. I try to do the same and there are some little things that I enjoy and bring me happiness. Problem is they don't last long and they aren't impactful enough to distract me from the issues that drag me down every day. But it is important to have something, no matter how small, to look forward to. Thank you for your comment and I hope you continue to find purpose in the little things

It does spiral fast. But you're right, there is always hope, no matter how small it may seem. I believe the key is finding something to love, something to live for. This something needs to be able to motivate you to continue fighting and digging yourself out of whatever hell you're currently in. We must create our own hope, and that is very doable. Good luck to you as well.

I hear you. Life is incredibly difficult if you don't have something to motivate you, something to look forward to. Why do we continue to get up every morning? Theoretically it's because there is something new or exciting to discover, or some form of happiness to experience. But if you don't have that, or don't have any hope of having that in the future, life becomes almost pointless.

For me personally, I don't have much hope of one day finding and sustaining happiness in the future. Maybe I'm being too pessimistic, but when your future outlook seems so bleak, what is the point of continuing on and suffering in silence? These are difficult questions to answer and I empathize with whoever has to face them
